title: Policy Form Provisions: Who May End a Medicare Supplement Policy, the Free Look Return, and Service Changes
content:
Only the policyholder may end a policy under Medicare Supplement Insurance Policies, because the contract and the premium are theirs; no relative, agent or provider may end it for them.

### The free look window

The policyholder returns the policy no later than the last day of the free look period counted from the policy effective date. The effective date is taken from the policy record, together with the policy and the reason its cover ended, and is read against that policy before the cancellation is recorded. Calendar days are counted from the day after the policy effective date, every day of the week counts, a return made on the final day is in time, and full 24-hour periods are never used in place of calendar days. The length of the period is the number of calendar days the plan letter carries as its free look period.

*Two hypothetical returns.* Where the free look period runs 30 calendar days, a policy returned on the thirtieth day after its effective date is returned on the final day and is in time; a policy returned on the thirty-first day is out of that window.

### The record the cancellation is made on

The cancellation is recorded on an underwriting file with a request to cancel the policy, or to return it inside the free look period, and an intake status of recorded, awaiting the applicant's signature, or under review. That file, the request it carries and the status it stands at are what settle this, correlated by the underwriting file itself, before the cancellation is taken.

### What each kind of ending does to the premium

A policy returned inside the free look period is treated as never having been bought: every penny of premium is returned, and any benefit already paid is recovered from the policyholder.

A cancellation outside the free look period takes effect at the end of the notice the plan letter requires, and premium paid beyond that date is returned on the plan letter's unearned premium basis.

### Two further matters

A policyholder cancelling because they are moving is told which of the plan's policies are sold where they are going, because a supplement is not always portable.

A change of payment method, billing frequency or discount does not end the policy and never restarts a waiting period; it takes effect from the next billing period.
